top.line: If you are looking for a job, act as that job
top.para: Dinis's most common advice to people looking for work: you have time, so act as the person in the job you want, for a startup, an open-source project or a company, and do it in public. He wrote it in 2018 too. Reach does not matter; a link does, because it lets people who want to help forward your work.

in-short.line: Time, action, publicity and a link
in-short.para: Looking for a job means having some time. Use it to do the job you want before you have the title, in startups, open source or companies you admire, and do it in public. Reach does not matter; linkable work lets helpers forward it. Put your CV online, and learn the small toolset that makes that possible.

time.line: Whatever the reason, you have time
time.para: People between jobs, out of university, newly arrived, back from maternity leave, or still employed with evenings free are all looking for work for different reasons. For most, the bottom line is the same: looking for a job means having time, and the best use of it is to act as the person in the job you want.

act.line: Do the work before you have the title
act.para: Someone Dinis met at a startup summit wanted to be a project manager but lacked the track record. His advice: start acting in the role, for a startup or open-source project, adding value, tagging them, sending ideas and connecting with their people. Good public work brings references, introductions, pay and sometimes the job, for any role, artist included.

2018.line: The same advice, eight years ago
2018.para: Dinis's 2018 book Generation Z Developers said it in its chapter on getting a job: collaborate on companies' open-source projects and act like you are part of the company, adding value. It also said nothing stops you doing this, which is truer in 2026, when the tools to do real work for a company before being hired are in everyone's hands.

public.line: Work that can be seen can be linked
public.para: Do the work where it can be seen: a public pull request, a post tagging the company, an article on your own site, an open project board. Private work helps the company; public work helps the company and you, because it can be linked.

reach.para: Dinis says he has less reach than people assume: most of his LinkedIn posts get a hundred views, sometimes five hundred, occasionally a thousand. Writing for reach leads to disappointment and stopping. Publish anyway, because the point is to have something to link, which changes what others can do for you.

help.para: Friends, former colleagues and people met at events want to help, but can do little with a general request. They can forward a link to work you did for a startup. So give them linkable work, a page about you and evidence they can pass on with one line, the same idea as an article behind every email.

cv.para: If you are looking for a job, your CV should be a page with links to the work that anyone can forward, not only a PDF sent on request. The 2018 book made the same case for developers in an outline: GitHub is your CV, because it shows how you work and collaborate.

bar.line: Learn the small skill that connects the rest
bar.para: If you cannot yet open a GitHub account, connect it to Claude or ChatGPT and have the agent build and edit a site, learn that first. It takes an afternoon, and your own newsroom shows one way by voice memo. It connects the work, the page that shows it and the people who can pass it on.

limits.para: This is advice from what Dinis has seen work, not a method with numbers. Not everyone has time, because of caring, second jobs or illness. Unpaid work can be exploited, so choose projects where the work is yours to show. The person from the summit is not named because she has not been asked.

sources.para: From Dinis's voice memo of 18 October 2026 and his 2018 book Generation Z Developers, its chapter on getting a job, read from the book's repository that day. Related articles cover hired for the workflow, the man behind the curtain, your own newsroom, explorer coding and the plan for the book's AI edition.
